findings.reason: a builder following §8 as written leaves a dispatch guard reading a foreign follower's health from a fact §8 proves does not cross nodes.
findings.text: §8 says `_follower_liveness` stays the single reader so "its other readers take the corrected value", but it corrects only the `live` field: `registered` (and the `released` field derived from it at follower_registration.py:606) still come from the node-local flock, which §8 itself shows reads free on every other node, so a live foreign follower still yields `released: True`, and that value flows through `watch_state` (watch_unit.py:205) into `session_follower_released`, which the dispatch admission at dispatch_watch.py:822 treats as "the follower can keep dispatching on a live watcher process" — the plan's premise that the shared reader fixes every consumer is false for this reader

findings.reason: §9's stated remedy addresses no cause it names and is inert until §8 lands, so a node built to §9's own words ships a hook line that recommends a no-op command.
findings.text: §9 rejects `--ensure` because it "changes nothing", then offers the follower arming line "the command that registers the session"; but the incident §9 describes is one where all live reckon followers are already registered (its sibling §8: "All four live reckon followers are registered from clu-2002"), so re-arming a registered follower also changes nothing, and produces a snapshot only once §8's corrected foreign-liveness judgement is present

findings.reason: the builder must either widen freshness's return beyond the stated single state or reintroduce the second seat read the section forbids, and a build that does neither fails §9's own done-when that the line names the host.
findings.text: §9 requires the hook line to "name that host" while also requiring that `freshness` "gains one state for this reading, so the hook does not judge the seat a second way"; `not_fresh_line` receives only `state: str` (coordinator_obligations.py:729), so the stated mechanism supplies a state and not the host, and the section forbids the hook from reading the seat itself

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol resolves: `runs.renew_producer_lease` (reckon/crew/runs.py:1764), `producer_lease_seconds` (runs.py:1702), `_follower_liveness` (reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:482), `seat_names_a_live_foreign_producer` (reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:143), `freshness` (reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:369), `not_fresh_line` (reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:729); the extensionless archive href resolves to the landed `.html` and its `#s3`/`#s4` anchors exist.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §8 and §9 each name a negative control that fails on the unfixed code (free-lock foreign registration reads gone under lock-judgement; missing snapshot reads no-producer), so neither measure can pass on the unbuilt code.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both controls are logged under the run directory and §8's post-merge check reads the crew home's obligations directory, all durable paths a later reader can open.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §8 and §9 name no new symbol by a plan label or ticket number, and the run ids and commit shas they cite are evidence data, not code names.
rubric_items.reasoning: findings — §8 corrects only `live` while a lock-derived `released` still reaches a dispatch guard; §9's remedy does not address the cause it names and its own line cannot carry the host it requires.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 carries one deliverable (a foreign follower judged by a renewed lease) and §9 one (the hook line for a missing snapshot beside a live foreign seat).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §9's deliverable depends on §8's corrected foreign-liveness judgement, but the carrying followup f-sheinr-002 declares the two "write different files and can run in parallel" and neither section declares the dependency.
